Project Overview

One enterprise story across six web experiences.

The project consisted of designing one Enterprise Homepage and five individual Business Landing Pages for Group Medical Insurance, Credit Insurance, Travel Insurance, Gig Worker Insurance, and Electronics Protection Insurance. Although every business served a different audience and use case, the experience needed to feel like one cohesive product.

Background

ACKO Enterprise had evolved. Its website hadn't.

The existing website had originally been created quickly, simply to establish an online presence and collect leads. As the Enterprise business matured, it needed to become much more than a marketing page — it needed to become the digital identity of the business. Here's what it was actually working against:

Generic messaging
Didn't align with ACKO's design language
Weak storytelling
Poor information hierarchy
Generic, AI-generated appearance
Didn't communicate credibility
Failed to reflect ACKO as technology-first
Looked like every other insurance website
Before
Generic, template-led presence
Generic messaging. Weak storytelling. Poor information hierarchy. Didn't communicate credibility or reflect ACKO as technology-first.
After
A cohesive digital identity
One design language, stronger hierarchy, unified storytelling, business-specific clarity, and an interface that could represent ACKO for Business at enterprise scale.
Business Goal

Not simply a redesign. A market position.

The goal was to establish ACKO Enterprise as a modern, technology-first insurance platform that enterprise decision makers could trust.

Research

Understanding both the users and the business.

Before designing anything, I conducted research by speaking with existing enterprise partners, potential partners, prospective customers, CHROs, CFOs, insurance brokers, and enterprise decision makers.

CHRO
Enterprise Buyer
CFO
Enterprise Buyer
Insurance Broker
Channel Partner
Enterprise Partner
Existing & Prospective
Decision Maker
Prospective Customer

Alongside external research, I spent time understanding each of the five enterprise businesses in depth. Rather than treating this as a website redesign, I approached it as designing the digital identity of an entire business ecosystem — to understand how enterprise buyers evaluate insurance partners, what builds trust, what information influences purchasing decisions, how each business differs, and how technology could become a differentiator.

Stakeholder Alignment

A three-day workshop, before a single screen was designed.

After research, I facilitated a three-day cross-functional workshop involving Product, Engineering, Design, Content, Marketing and SEO — to align everyone on one shared vision before moving into design.

This wasn't the only alignment point. Working with broad business objectives and periodic stakeholder feedback throughout the project, I translated research into a clear experience strategy — and later used a working prototype, not a deck, to bring leadership onto the same page on creative direction.

The Design Challenge

There wasn't a predefined blueprint.

This wasn't simply a redesign exercise. Working with broad business objectives and periodic stakeholder feedback, I translated research into a clear experience strategy, established the creative direction, and drove the project from concept to launch. I also wanted to challenge a larger industry pattern.

What the category defaults to
  • Heavy text
  • Corporate imagery
  • Stock illustrations
  • Static layouts
  • Nothing memorable
What ACKO needed to feel like
  • Modern
  • Interactive
  • Technology-first
  • Premium & confident
  • Memorable
The Big Idea

One of my strengths is rapid prototyping and interaction design.

Instead of using animation as decoration, I explored a concept where a central 3D metaphor object became the storytelling anchor of the website — guiding users through the experience while reinforcing the narrative across different sections.

01
A central 3D object as the anchor
Rather than decorative motion, one object carried the narrative — reappearing and reshaping as the story moved from section to section.
02
Scroll-driven storytelling
To elevate the experience further, I designed scroll-driven storytelling, motion-led transitions, micro interactions, rich visual storytelling and immersive product exploration.
03
Prototyped before development
Before any development began, I built a high-fidelity interactive prototype entirely in Figma — allowing leadership to experience the vision before engineering investment.
04
Alignment in a single sitting
The concept received immediate alignment and became the creative foundation for the project — proof over pitch.
Figma Concept
that aligned everyone
Execution

Six experiences. One consistent language.

I designed all six experiences — the homepage and five business landing pages — while maintaining a consistent design language, interaction system and storytelling framework across every business.

Throughout execution, I worked closely with the Product Manager, Developers, Motion Designer, Visual Designer, Content Designer, Marketing and SEO. As the primary point of contact, I ensured consistency across design, content, motion and implementation while driving the project through to launch.
